STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.claim: A different reported view says verses 53–59 were all revealed concerning Waḥshī.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.anchor: while others say that vv. 53–59 were all revealed in regard to it

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.claim: The call to repent in verses 54–67 leads into the final extended contrast between the believers’ and disbelievers’ ends in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.anchor: This is followed by an exhortation to turn to God in repentance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.claim: Rather than despairing of God or seeking deities and intercessors, people should turn to the forgiving and merciful God in every circumstance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.anchor: losing hope in God and seeking other deities and intercessors is not the correct way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.claim: People should turn to God and believe in His revealed Book before He seizes them; later regret and a wish to believe will be too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.anchor: before He seizes them, people should turn to Him and profess faith in this magnificent Book

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r17.claim: فأكون can be parsed as the response to a wish signaled by لو, with hidden أن, or coordinated with كرة, where being is itself wished for; poetry illustrates the constructions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r17.anchor: وانتصب فأكون على جواب التمني الدال عليه لو، أو على كرة، إذ هو مصدر، فيكون مثل قوله: فما لك منها غير ذكرى وحسرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r1.claim: With fa as the response to a wish, hidden أن is obligatory and being follows from the wished return; coordinated with كرة, أن may be explicit or hidden and being is itself wished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r1.anchor: والفرق بينهما أن الفاء إذا كانت في جواب التمني، كانت أن واجبة الإضمار، وكان الكون مترتبا على حصول المتمنى، لا متمنى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r2.claim: When fa coordinates with karratan, أن may be explicit or implicit and the state itself can be wished, unlike the response-to-wish parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r2.anchor: وإذا كانت للعطف على كرة، جاز إظهار أن وإضمارها، وكان الكون متمنى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the sinner's three statements retain their order—regret, excuse about guidance, then wish to return—and the reply answers the one requiring an answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.anchor: وهو أنه حكى أقوال النفس على ترتيبها ونظمها، ثم أجاب من بينها عما اقتضى الجواب.

SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r1.claim: One parse coordinates فأكون with the verbal noun كرة: becoming virtuous is itself wished; cited poetry illustrates such coordination.
SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r1.anchor: أحدهما: عطفه على " كرة " فإنها مصدر، فعطف مصدر مؤول على مصدر مصرح به

SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r2.claim: Alternatively, فأكون is subjunctive as the consequence of the understood wish in لو أن لي كرة; becoming virtuous follows the wished-for return, so أن is implicit.
SAMIN-DURR:39:58/r2.anchor: على جواب التمني المفهوم من قوله: { لو أن لي كرة }.

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r13.claim: The following speeches likewise name what people would regret saying; God had already made the paths of guidance clear, and a living person capable of discernment has been given the proof.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r13.anchor: أي وكراهة أن تقول هذا القول الذي يؤدي

ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n61/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n61/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n61/r1.claim: Asad points to parallels concerning regret and wishing for another chance.
ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n61/r1.anchor: Cf. 2:167 and 26:102, as well as 6:27-28 and the corresponding note 19.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p568/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p568/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p568/r2.claim: On seeing the torment, the person wishes to return to worldly life and become among those grateful to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p568/r2.anchor: so that they could become among those grateful to God.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r1.claim: Karra means a return to worldly life.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r2.claim: The hoped-for excellence would be in both creed and deeds.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.claim: Law expresses a wish, and fa-akūna is subjunctive after the fa answering that wish.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r3.anchor: و ( لو ) للتمني ( فأكون ) منصوب في جوابها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r4.claim: Al-Bahr also permits the subjunctive to coordinate with karra, which is a verbal noun, citing two poetic parallels; with fa as the wish's answer, an is obligatorily omitted and excellence follows the wished return, while coordination allows optional omission and makes excellence itself part of the wish.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p18#2/r4.anchor: وجوز في البحر أن يكون منتصبا بالعطف على ( كرة )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.claim: The soul sees the punishment directly, face to face.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.anchor: حين ترى العذاب} عيانا، {لو أن لي كرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r3.claim: Karra means a return to worldly life.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r4.claim: The good-doers here are those who affirm God's oneness.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:57-59/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:57-59/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:57-59/r2.claim: On seeing punishment, the speaker wishes to return and become good in belief and conduct; the alternatives show futile vacillation and excuses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:57-59/r2.anchor: في العقيدة والعمل، وأو للدلالة على أنها لا تخلوا من هذه الأقوال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r1.claim: The wish follows the soul’s admission of falsehood and resort to fabrication, adding a futile wish that only increases its loss.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r1.anchor: فقال : { أو تقول } أي تلك النفس المفرطة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r2.claim: The heedless soul wishes for a return to the abode of deeds so it can act and become one of those who do good.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r2.anchor: أي رجعة إلى دار العمل لأتمكن منه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r3.claim: He parses “so I might be” as coordinated with the response to the wish; this parsing best fits the following verses.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p464/r3.anchor: هذا الإعراب - وهو عطفه على الجواب - أوفق لبقية الآيات

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God foretells what people will say and do before they say or know it, linking this to 35:14.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى على ما فرطت} الآيات قال أخبر الله سبحانه ما العباد قائلون قبل أن يقولوه

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r8.claim: Qatāda assigns the wish to return to worldly life to a third group.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r8.anchor: قال: لو رجعت إلى الدنيا قال: هذا قول صنف آخر

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues returned people still could not attain guidance and would repeat former conduct, citing 6:28 and 6:110.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى على ما فرطت

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.claim: Qatāda says the three regrets belong to different classes of people.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.anchor: قال: هذا قول صنف منهم {أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين} قال: هذا قول صنف منهم آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r3.claim: The wish made upon seeing the punishment is an unqualified wish; law functions as a particle of wishing, and fa-akun is subjunctive as its response.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r4.claim: Karra means a return, specifically back to earthly life to do good; this wish admits that the speaker formerly did evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r4.anchor: وهذا اعتراف بأنها علمت أنها كانت من المسيئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.claim: The statements follow the natural movement of thought at judgment: regret, then excuse, then wish for a return to do good. Reordering them would lose the signal of how these thoughts arise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.anchor: الأصل في الإنشاء ما لم يوجد ما يقتضي العدول عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.claim: The reply pairs the guidance excuse with signs that came and were denied, neglect with the greater offense of arrogance, and the wish to be God-fearing with being a disbeliever; Quranic guidance left no excuse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.anchor: أن الله هداك في الدنيا بالإرشاد بآيات القرآن فقابلت الإرشاد بالتكذيب والاستكبار والكفر بها فلا عذر لك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.claim: The answer uses a deliberately scrambled distribution after a summary: it first dispatches the main excuse, then neglect, then the return wish. It skips the mockery claim because that was already an admission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.anchor: وكان الجواب على طريقة النشر المشوش بعد اللف رعيا لمقتضى ذلك التشويش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.claim: The two later occurrences of aw taqūlu coordinate with the first an taqūla clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.anchor: وقوله: أو تقول في الموضعين عطف على قوله: أن تقول الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r13.claim: Karra is the verbal noun of karra-yakurr, to return.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r13.anchor: و: كرة مصدر من كر يكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r14.claim: Fa-akūna is subjunctive under an implicit an and coordinates to karra, with the verb construed as a verbal noun; al-Farrāʾ cites a parallel poetic construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r14.anchor: وقوله: فأكون نصب بأن مضمرة مقدرة، وهو عطف على قول: كرة والمراد: لو أن لي كرة فكونا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r15.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r15.claim: Al-Ṭabarī gives the construction as meaning that the speaker could return and then become one of the doers of good; this is a wish.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r15.anchor: وقد قرر بعض الناس الكلام: أنه لي أن أكر فأكون، ذكره الطبري، وهذا الكون في هذه الآية داخل في التمني

BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r3.claim: The punishment is seen plainly and directly.
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r3.anchor: {أو تقول حين ترى العذاب} . عيانا ومشاهدة.

BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r4.claim: Here law expresses a wish: if only I had another chance.

BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r5.claim: Karra means a return to worldly life; kara ʿalayhi means turn toward him, kara ʿanhu means return from him, and karra also means one time.
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r5.anchor: {كرة} رجعة إلى الدنيا يقال : كر عليه عطف ، وعنه رجع. والكره المرة.

BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r6.claim: The verb is subjunctive as the response to the wish.

BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r7.claim: The hoped-for excellence would be in both belief and action.

BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r8.claim: The conjunction indicates that people will make these statements in bewilderment, excuses, and useless regret; alternatively, different groups make different statements.
BURSEVI:v8p97#2/r8.anchor: واو للدلالة على أنها لا تخلو عن هذه الأقوال تحيرا وتعللا بما لا طائل تحته وندما ، حيث لا ينفع. وقيل : إن قوما يقولون : هذا. وقوما يقولون : ذاك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r4.claim: The condemned person wishes he had been guided and God-fearing, or that he could return to worldly life and act well.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r4.anchor: أي: تود أن لو (2) أعيدت إلى الدار فتحسن (3) العمل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God disclosed what people would say before they said it and what they would do before acting; Ibn Kathir cites 35:14 in support.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة: عن ابن عباس: أخبر الله سبحانه (4) ، ما العباد قائلون قبل أن يقولوه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r6.claim: God says that even if the condemned were returned, they would not follow guidance but would resume what they were forbidden, and their claim is false.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r6.anchor: فأخبر الله تعالى: أن لو ردوا لما قدروا على الهدى، وقال تعالى: {ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون}

MUQATIL:39:55-60/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r7.claim: A return is a return to worldly life; the speaker would do good, meaning become a monotheist.
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r7.anchor: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة } يعنى رجعة إلى الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#4/r1.claim: Karra means a return to worldly life; the speaker wishes to become one of the people of faith and good works, that is, monotheists.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة ﴾ رجعة إلى الدنيا ﴿ فأكون من المحسنين ﴾ من الموحدين

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r3.claim: Karra means a return to worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r3.anchor: لو أن لي كرة } أي رجعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r4.claim: Fa-akūna is subjunctive as the response to a wish; alternatively it is coordinated with karra because the latter means “that I return.”
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r4.anchor: { فأكون } نصب على جواب التمني، وإن شئت كان معطوفا على { كرة } لأن معناها أن أكر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī cites the line about wearing an abaya and finding comfort as an example of coordination with an implied “that I.”
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r5.anchor: للبْس عباءة وتقر عيني أحب إلي من لبس الشفوف

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a line where “and you ask” is coordinated with “remembering,” since the phrase means that one has nothing but to remember and ask where the riders went.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r6.anchor: فمالك منها غير ذكرى وخشية وتسأل عن ركبانها أين يمموا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.claim: Qatāda distinguishes three groups: one regrets neglecting God’s affair, another says God should have guided it, and the third wishes for another return to become righteous.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: هؤلاء أصناف صنف منهم قال: { يحسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله }.

STUDYQURAN:39:58/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:58/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:58/r1.claim: Unlike the prior verse's blame of God, this soul acknowledges some culpability and asks for a second chance, as do the guilty in 32:12.
STUDYQURAN:39:58/r1.anchor: those represented in this verse acknowledge some culpability and ask to be given a second chance, as in 32:12

STUDYQURAN:39:58/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:58/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:58/r2.claim: Such pleas are insincere and useless because revelation was given and respite lasted until death; even if returned, they would again do what they were forbidden, and are called liars in 6:28.
STUDYQURAN:39:58/r2.anchor: such lamentations are not considered sincere and are of no avail, for even if they were sent back, they would return to the very thing they had been forbidden

TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says people condemned in pre-Islamic times considered following Muhammad but thought God and His Messenger would not accept them; the revelation continued through 39:58.
TAB-FULL:v20p226/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} [الزمر: 53] الآية، قال: " كان قوم مسخوطين

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.claim: The commands to repent and submit aim to prevent three afterlife regrets: sorrow for neglect, a claim that God did not guide, and a wish to return and act righteously.
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.anchor: الله، وأن لا تقول نفس لأخرى: لو أن الله هداني للحق، فوفقني للرشاد

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r3.claim: When confronted with God's punishment, the soul wishes for a return to worldly life so it could be among those who obey God and do what the messengers commanded.
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r3.anchor: تقول لو أن لي رجعة إلى الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.claim: Qatada assigns the first regret to one class of people, the plea “if God had guided me” to a second, and the wish to return to a third.
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله} الآية، قال: «هذا قول صنف منهم» {أو تقول لو أن الله هداني}

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God revealed what people would say before they said it; their claim that they would be guided if returned is false, since God would again prevent their guidance as before (35:14; 6:28, 110).
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله} قال: " أخبر الله ما العباد قائلوه قبل أن يقولوه

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r6.claim: One parse makes “I would then be” subjunctive as the apodosis of “if only I had a return.”
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r6.anchor: وفي نصب قوله {فأكون} [الزمر: 58] وجهان: أحدهما: أن يكون نصبه على أنه جواب لو

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r7.claim: Alternatively, “I would then be” coordinates with the syntactic position of “return,” construed as “if only I could return”; a parallel poem coordinates “you ask” with “remembrance.”
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r7.anchor: والثاني: على الرد على موضع الكرة وتوجيه الكرة في المعنى إلى: لو أن لي أن أكر، كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الطويل]

TAB-FULL:v20p236#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p236#2/r1.claim: In the cited poem, “you ask” is accusative and coordinated with the underlying sense of “remembrance,” since the meaning is “you have only remembrance and asking.”
TAB-FULL:v20p236#2/r1.anchor: فنصب تسأل عطفا بها على موضع الذكرى، لأن معنى الكلام: فما لك غير أن تذكر وتسأل

TABATABAI:39:53/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.claim: The passage calls people to Islam and following revelation, warns of regret for excess and worldly arrogance, and contrasts the pious’ salvation with unbelievers’ loss; its tone conveys mercy.
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يدعوهم إلى الإسلام واتباع ما أنزل الله ويحذرهم عما يستعقبه إسرافهم

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.claim: These seven verses form one connected discourse: the ban on despair prepares for the following calls to repentance, submission, and righteous action, so the first verse is not an isolated promise.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.anchor: كلام واحد ذو سياق واحد متصل ينهى عن القنوط

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r8.claim: Law expresses a wish and karra means return: seeing the punishment, the soul wishes to return to worldly life and become righteous.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r8.anchor: لو للتمني والكرة الرجعة، والمعنى أو تقول نفس متمنية حين ترى العذاب

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r3.claim: When they are brought to the Fire and see it, they wish to return to worldly life and believe, as in 6:27 and 23:107.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r3.anchor: ثم إذا أمروا بدخول النار فأوقفوا عليها ثم ادخلوا فيها تمنوا الرجوع إلى الدنيا ليحسنوا فيها

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.claim: The three sayings follow the order in which criminals would utter them; moving the reply to connect directly with its target would disrupt the arrangement.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.anchor: ثم لما نقل الأقوال على ما بينها من الترتيب أخذ في الجواب ولو أخر القول المجاب عنه حتى يتصل بالجواب

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.claim: God does not answer the first and third sayings, about mocking truth and wishing to return, because He rebuffs the criminals and forbids them to speak, as 23:106–111 shows.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.anchor: لأن في الأول حديث استهزائهم بالحق وأهله وفي الثالث تمنيهم للرجوع إلى الدنيا والله سبحانه يزجر هؤلاء يوم القيامة

TABRISI:39:56-60/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56-60/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56-60/r9.claim: The speaker wishes for return to worldly life and to become monotheist and obedient.
TABRISI:39:56-60/r9.anchor: أي لو أن لي رجعة إلى الدنيا فأكون من الموحدين المطيعين

FARRA:v2p421/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p421/r7.claim: فأكون is subjunctive as the response to لو; alternatively, it coordinates with an implied أن inside the meaning of كرة.
FARRA:v2p421/r7.anchor: النصب في قوله (فأكون) جواب للو. وإن شئت جعلته مردودا على تأويل أن، تضمرها في الكرة

THALABI:v8p246/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p246/r13.claim: The lost person imagines that divine guidance would have made him God-fearing, then wishes for another return to worldly life so he could be among the virtuous.
THALABI:v8p246/r13.anchor: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين أو تقول حين ترى العذاب

THALABI:v8p246/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p246/r14.claim: Thaʿlabi says there are two analyses for the accusative of fa-akūna, but this excerpt does not supply them.

ELMALILI:39:56-63/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r4.claim: On seeing the punishment, a soul will wish for another return so that it could become one of the good-doers.
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r4.anchor: Bana bir geri dönmek olsa idi de muhsinlerden olsa idim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:57/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:57/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:57/r1.claim: The disbeliever’s wish for another chance to become righteous after seeing punishment will go unanswered; the following verse gives the reason.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:57/r1.anchor: “Keşke bana bir fırsat daha tanınsa da iyilerden biri olsam!” şeklindeki temennisinin (58. âyet) karşılıksız kalacağı ifade edilmekte

ITQAN:v2p329/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p329/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p329/r3.claim: Al-muḥsinīn is glossed as the guided ones.

NAHHAS:v4p18/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p18/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p18/r1.claim: فأكون is accusative as the response to a wish, or may coordinate with كرة because the sense is أن أكون; a poetic line illustrates it.
NAHHAS:v4p18/r1.anchor: نصب على جواب التمني فإن شئت كان معطوفا على كرة لأن معناه أن أكون كما قال

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.claim: The next section warns that polytheism and intercession will not save the idolaters but hasten ruin; success requires sincere turning to God and following His revealed Book, or their later regret will be useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.anchor: The path to success hinges on focussing attention towards God with sincerity of heart and on following this best of Books
